subject: Edge proxy / egress controls — request for pen test evidence and boundary mapping (FinHealth)
messages:
From: FinHealth SecOps <secops@finhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: edge proxy attack surface + pen test evidence for private VPC deployment

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing for our vendor risk review and need more detail about the penetration test coverage for Redwood's private VPC deployments. Specifically, FinHealth would like:

- A clear boundary diagram showing what lives in the customer VPC vs. Redwood-managed control plane (we need to validate there are no shared control-plane segments in-scope).
- The most recent penetration test report (redacted as necessary) that covers the edge/proxy layer used for private deployments, including any findings related to egress rules, bastion/management hosts, and TLS termination.
- A CSV or list of the egress firewall/security-group rules applied to the private deployment for validation against our network policies.
- Status of remediation for any high/critical findings that could impact our environment.

Please indicate expected delivery date and any NDA or redaction constraints. We may share the artifacts with our third-party assessor (OptimaSec) under our data handling agreement.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Security Engineer
FinHealth

---

Attachment: FinHealth_PenReqChecklist.xlsx (referenced)

Deliverable target: EOD 2027-01-17 pending approvals. If that timing doesn't work, we can push a preliminary package earlier.

Best,

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: FinHealth — required pen test artifacts (edge/proxy)

Team — FinHealth is requesting VPC-specific artifacts relating to private deployments. Please collect the items below and attach them to the shared Drive folder linked in the related_links field: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FinHealth/pen-evidence-2027-01

Requested items (priority order):
1) Boundary mapping: logical diagram that annotates which components run in the customer VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane. Include notes on traffic flows (inbound, outbound) and TLS termination points. (owner: Neha)
2) Redacted penetration test report that covers the edge proxy used for private deployments. We should remove customer-specific IPs and internal ticket IDs but keep technical findings and remediation notes. (owner: Diego)
3) Egress rules export (CSV) for the deployed VPC configuration as of 2027-01-10. Include security group / NACL rules and any managed firewall policies. (owner: Diego)
4) Remediation tracker: short summary table of any high/critical findings from the last two pen tests and current status (open/mitigated/verified). Include dates and JIRA IDs where applicable. (owner: Neha)

Constraints and asks:
- If the report contains vendor-supplied exploit code or PoCs, redact per our legal guidance and annotate redaction in the report.
- Do not include internal HR or payroll data — only infra/security artifacts.

Diego — can you confirm whether the pen test covered the customer-side edge proxy configuration (e.g., whether the proxy sits in the customer subnet versus an overlay) or if our tests targeted the Redwood-managed entry points only? I remember there was a mixed-scope engagement in Nov 2026.

Please upload drafts by 2027-01-16 EOD so I can do a final review before sending to FinHealth on the 17th.

Thanks — Tessa

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 11:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: FinHealth — required pen test artifacts (edge/proxy)

Tessa / team — status update and what I'm uploading to the Drive: 

1) Boundary mapping (attached: redwood_private_vpc_boundary_mapping_v1.png) — this is a logical diagram with notes showing that TLS terminates at the customer-managed edge proxy when customers opt for BYO-proxy; otherwise TLS terminates at our managed load balancer. Diagram includes a callout for managed control-plane endpoints (no shared data plane subnets).

2) Pen test report (attached: redwood_pen_test_report_2026-11_redacted.pdf) — November 2026 engagement. Scope: Redwood-managed edge services + optional customer-edge proxy patterns. We redacted IP-level identifiers and internal ticket metadata. Key items: two medium findings related to a proxy header parsing edge case (CVSS 6.2) — both have configuration mitigations and one advisory code fix scheduled in Feb 2027. No high/critical findings for egress.

3) Egress rules export (attached: egress_rules_export_20270110.csv) — includes SG/NACL rows and a short mapping to documented policies. Note: some enterprise customers implement supplemental egress controls in their own VPCs; the export is Redwood's default policy for private deployments.

4) Remediation tracker (uploaded as a spreadsheet in Drive) — shows the medium proxy parsing items as "mitigated via config" on 2027-01-11 and code fix targeted for 2027-02-10; verification planned after the code release by our QA team.

Regarding scope: the Nov 2026 pen test intentionally exercised both the Redwood-managed edge and the customer-provided proxy configuration via a test harness; OptimaSec was engaged as a third-party assessor for parts of the scope. I can provide an explicit scope table in the report front-matter if FinHealth wants it called out.

If you want a more detailed timeline for the fix, I can push a developer note from the runtime team (I spoke with Marcus Lin) — but that will add 24–48 hours.

- Diego
Principal Infra Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_boundary_mapping_v1.png; redwood_pen_test_report_2026-11_redacted.pdf; egress_rules_export_20270110.csv
